fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Why \"Amen\" May Be the Name of a Hidden God", "body": "The episode opens on a question Chance Garton says he put to his own father: why do Christians say amen at the end of a prayer? Dylan Saccoccio argues the word is not a Hebrew formula of assent but the name Ammon, written in Etruscan and Phoenician as the bare consonants O-M-N, with the vowel filled in later. He contends it sits closer to the Latin omen than to anything Semitic, and that the so-called kingdom of Ammon near modern Israel is a misattribution for a system he traces to the Italian peninsula."}, {"title": "Esotericism and the Useful Lies of the Ancients", "body": "Chance lays out a long case that ancient priests and philosophers hid their real doctrines on purpose, for defense against charges of heresy or atheism, and for social stability. He cites the noble lie of Plato's Republic and the Athenian doctrine of autochthony, the claim that ancestors sprang from the soil with the tools of their caste already in hand, as a story that justified conquest and kept the lower castes in place. He collects mottoes from Ovid, from Epicurus, and from Bishop Synesius of Cyrene, who advised loving wisdom at home and embracing fables abroad, alongside Proverbs 25:2."}, {"title": "Charles Blount, Robert Taylor, and the Lord Who Is Not God", "body": "Chance reads at length from Charles Blount's 1680 Great Is Diana of the Ephesians, on how princes governed an unruly creature through hope and fear, raising in the conscience what Blount calls a whip of torture, the fear of future punishment. Dylan then turns to Robert Taylor's Astronomico-Theological Lectures, written in prison, and to Taylor's warning never to confound the Lord with God. Taylor treats them as particular and general terms, reading Judges 11:24 and Jephthah's bargain with the children of Ammon as evidence that each nation claimed its own tutelary planet rather than a universal deity."}, {"title": "Yova, Adonai and the Sun That Hides in Winter", "body": "The thumbnail quote is Psalm 89:46, which Dylan renders not as Lord but as Jove or Yova, how long will you hide. He derives the name from hava, to fall or to become, the same letters read elsewhere as Eve and as life, separated only by context. From Adonai the hosts move to Adonis, following Taylor's claim that Adon is the same as Baal, the Lord common to Jupiter, Bacchus, Apollo and Osiris. Chance walks through the Adonis myth, Myrrha turned into the myrrh tree, the buried seed, the fostering by Persephone, and a death and resurrection."}, {"title": "Horns, Precession, and the Etruscan Origin Thesis", "body": "Chance reads Godfrey Higgins sorting bull headed gods from ram headed ones as successive precessional ages, Taurus giving way to Aries, with the Alexander coin bearing the horns of Ammon and a bull horned Buddha from Persia. Dylan counters that the horns may track local herding instead, and offers the Italian malocchio, bull horns hung over shops to ward off evil, as the root of the rock and roll hand sign. He closes on method, arguing that translation forces liberties nobody should cling to, and that his aim is forcing the status quo to concede it does not know."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: What if everything you’ve been told about religion and history is just the surface layer of a deeper, hidden truth? In this electrifying episode of Inner Whirled, Chance Garton and Dylan Saccoccio peel back the veils of secrecy to reveal the concealed doctrines that shaped the ancient world. From the esoteric significance of Jupiter Ammon to the hidden solar origins of monotheism, we explore how sacred knowledge has been encoded and obscured for millennia.
fields.Intro Paragraph 2: This episode covers why the ancients deliberately hid divine knowledge, the concealed astrotheology behind religious texts, the noble lie of how deception shaped civilizations, and whether "The Lord" was a hidden astronomical reference.

fields.Plus Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "One Sun Behind a Thousand Names", "body": "Robert Taylor's reading and Augustine's City of God both converge on the same claim: Jehovah, Baal, Adonis, Apollo, Osiris, Bacchus and Jupiter Ammon are not separate deities but epithets for the sun in its different phases, rising, setting, hidden in winter, reborn at Easter. Later in the segment, Chance reads Taylor's own line that Jehovah, Jupiter, Osiris and the rest were never separate gods but different names for one and the same deity, dismissing academic historians who call them distinct pagan gods as simply wrong about the aspects and epithets of a single Lord. Albert Pike's line about Brahma, Mithras, Osiris and Adonis becoming personifications of the sun is read as confirming the same pattern rather than proving a Masonic conspiracy."}, {"title": "Why the Ancients Hid the Truth on Purpose", "body": "Robert Fludd's own persecution for defending the weapon salve becomes Chance's case study in defensive esotericism, concealing accurate knowledge of nature and even certain technologies because the vulgar, fearful of what they do not understand, cannot be reasoned with. Augustine's City of God is read the same way, showing that educated pagans worshiped one God under many functions while common worshipers mistook the parts for separate gods. Dylan and Chance extend this into modern life, arguing that people still believe what flatters them and that trying to correct them only brings hardship, which is why esoteric writing protected both the teacher and the society."}, {"title": "The Zodiac Hidden Inside the Bible", "body": "Long stretches of this segment retranslate familiar verses as sky watching rather than history. The everlasting arms of Deuteronomy become the claws of Cancer, Joshua's sun standing still becomes the solstice, and the fall of Jericho's walls becomes the sun's descent into Leo after the crab. Sol Invictus and the Roman festival of the unconquered sun are tied directly to Easter's springtime date, and Isaiah's God that hidest thyself is matched to Osiris and Adonis as another name for the same seasonal disappearance and return of the sun that the whole episode calls Amen."}, {"title": "Doubting Official History, From Israel to Atlantis", "body": "Chance argues numismatic evidence shows no ancient coinage belonging to an Israelite kingdom, so the modern conflict over the region rests on a founding myth rather than documented history, similar to Plato's noble lie about Athenians born from the soil. The same skepticism is applied to the supposed Venetian language, whose oldest surviving text turns out to be a Greek translation of a Phoenician work that only surfaced in the 1500s and now sits, unexplained, in a French museum, and to DNA studies of Etruscan tombs that match modern Germans and Cornish people rather than a Near Eastern origin, all treated as evidence that accepted timelines were written to serve later political and religious agendas."}, {"title": "God as Hide and Seek", "body": "Late in the recording the etymology gives way to reflection. Robert Fludd's defense of the weapon salve becomes a case for action at a distance as evidence of an active but concealed God, and the omphalos stone wrapped in a serpent is read as the same hidden, waiting divinity found in a third trimester womb. The episode closes on Taylor's account of blind man's buff as a mock ritual of seeking a God who never forces belief, and on the idea that God stays hidden because forcing certainty would remove the choice a loving father wants his children to keep."}]

fields.Quotes JSON: [{"text": "You ever wonder why Christians say amen at the end of their prayer?", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "If you can read Etruscan, you can read Amen. It just looks like O-M-N, and that is literally closer to omen.", "author": "Dylan Saccoccio", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/0d1bec4c-36ec-4ba4-a1cb-9de0908b2433/Dylan-Saccoccio.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "Simply telling a student the answers, especially through writing, was more harmful than helpful, but leaving breadcrumbs to be deciphered would bring the student into true wisdom and knowledge.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "Why would God, the creator of this world, who can destroy and remake it, worry about priests and false prophets?", "author": "Dylan Saccoccio", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/0d1bec4c-36ec-4ba4-a1cb-9de0908b2433/Dylan-Saccoccio.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "You see with the coins of the ancient world that the modern scholars tell us represent this ruler or that king or that queen, when clearly the symbolism is religious symbolism.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "There's no nation in the world that ever called themselves Phoenicians or any of that stuff. That name comes from Greeks.", "author": "Dylan Saccoccio", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/0d1bec4c-36ec-4ba4-a1cb-9de0908b2433/Dylan-Saccoccio.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "If Dylan's research points to the truth about that, then the whole Genesis story does seem to be an Etruscan story.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "I think everybody getting to that base level of conceding we don't know will be more valuable for us as a whole than everybody fighting over what they think is true.", "author": "Dylan Saccoccio", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/0d1bec4c-36ec-4ba4-a1cb-9de0908b2433/Dylan-Saccoccio.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}]
fields.Title: Amen's Hidden Meaning: The Secret God Ammon & Ancient Astrotheology
